Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with a few days of stinging pain on urination (dysuria).
Chief_Complaint.source_text: it's, it's uh, hurting when I, , when I use the bathroom, when I pee... it's sort of like a stinging kind of pain.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Associated with lower abdominal cramping pain.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I also maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lower down in my tummy... sort of, sort of cramping.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient noticed a small amount of blood in the urine (hematuria) earlier today.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: there was a little bit of blood earlier today

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The urine has an unusual or weird smell.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it does kind of, it, it kind of like, doesn't smell very, it smells a bit weird I guess

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies urinary frequency, nausea, vomiting, or fever.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: have you found yourself going to the toilet more often than normal? Um, not, I don't think so... have you noticed any other symptoms like nausea, vomiting? Uh, no, not , not at all... any fevers or temperatures? No, no, no fever, no.
are your bowels working OK? Um, uh, I think so, yeah

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient tried over-the-counter bicarbonate with no relief.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: try some uh, over the counter bicarbonate, to try and help with the pain but it wasn't, it wasn't really helping.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Past_Medical_History.source_text: in the past I've had some uh, some IBS.

Medications.source_text: Do you take any regular medications? Uh, no

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient is allergic to Clindamycin, which causes swelling.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Uh, yeah, I'm allergic to, Clindamycin... I, I get some like a, a, a swelling, basically.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a 19-year-old student studying biology.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: My name is Jessica Smith, and I'm nineteen years old... I'm a student... I'm studying biology.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is sexually active with one partner for the past two months and uses condoms for contraception.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I've had a boyfriend for about a, a couple of months now... we use condoms.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has never had an STD screen.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: When was your last um, uh, last STD screen? If, if ever? Don't think I've ever, I don't think I've ever had one.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Last menstrual period was a couple of weeks ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: When was your last, period? Uh, couple of weeks ago.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient lives in a flat with friends.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I live in a, live in a flat near my college, with a, a couple of like friends of mine.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially on weekends.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I don't, I don't smoke, uh, I do drink, like on the weekends, yeah.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has no relevant family history.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: In terms of your family history, is there anything I should be aware of... Uh, no I don't think so

Assessment.content: The impression is a simple urinary tract infection (UTI) / cystitis.
Assessment.source_text: I think probably do have what we call a simple UTI or urinary tract infection, bladder infection

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics, either Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim (one tablet twice a day).
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I'll give you a course of antibiotics today. Something, called either Nitrofurantoin, or Trimethoprim. Uh, and it's normally a three day course. Uh, so, one tablet, twice a day, for three days.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to increase fluid intake and try cranberry juice.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids... You can try, cranberry juice

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to perform a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy if symptoms persist.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I'd always , advise getting a pregnancy test, to rule out pregnancy.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Yeah I mean if you can try and avoid it, I think that'd be sensible.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to call back or return for review at the end of the week (after 3 days) if symptoms are not better.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised on red flag symptoms for urgent review: high temperatures, back pain, or feeling generally more unwell (to rule out kidney infection).
Follow_up_Information.source_text: And things to look out for would be, you know, if you are having kind of, high temperatures, a back pain, um just , generally feeling more unwell... we do worry whether your infection may be spreading up towards your kidneys
